exposure: prior abdominal surgery history (gynecologic, gastrointestinal, biliopancreatic)
outcome: conversion to open or conventional laparoscopic surgery
cohort: The study included 768 patients who underwent gynecologic robotic surgery at Yamanashi Central Hospital between April 2018 and March 2023.
finding: Abdominal wall adhesions, especially in patients with a history of abdominal surgery, led to significantly longer operative times in gynecologic robotic surgery and required trocar placement adjustments in some cases, although estimated blood loss did not differ significantly and conversions to open surgery were avoided due to the robot's flexibility.
